correctness.rationale: With four distinct observations the original allocation has the largest absolute two-versus-two mean contrast exactly when the two X values are both below or both above the two Y values. Standardized partition contrasts reduce rejection to the isotropic cone |Z₁|>a|U|+b|V|, whose trihedral solid angle gives the closed formula. Symmetry and strict concavity give the unique minimum and endpoint limit. Fresh simulations with 600,000 draws at each ratio 1, 4 and 100 agreed within 0.31 Monte Carlo standard errors.

originality.rationale: Unequal-variance failure of the unstudentized permutation mean test is classical. Murphy is the strongest historical overlap risk because it reports simulated size curves, but its accessible abstract does not expose an exact two-by-two Gaussian closed form, and full text could not be verified. Modern robust-permutation sources establish the phenomenon and remedies but not this solid-angle formula. Best-of-knowledge originality passes with the Murphy-table risk explicit.

value.rationale: This is the smallest balanced design with a nontrivial exact two-sided rejection. The exact curve and sharp limiting inflation quantify a real weak-null calibration failure and give a clean benchmark for studentized or robust permutation methods.

final_claim: For the ordinary two-sided permutation mean test with two Gaussian observations per group, equal means and variance ratio k, the rejection probability at the smallest attainable level one third is the stated arctangent curve, uniquely minimized at equal variances and tending to one half at extreme variance ratios.
limitations: Two observations per group, Gaussian data, unstudentized absolute mean difference and level one third only.
